title: support systemd-homed's "forget keys on suspend"
line: With systemd-homed's lock-on-suspend enabled, waking the computer now shows the login screen, and logging in there unlocks the home folder and returns to the running session.
explanation: With pam_systemd_home's suspend option, systemd-sleep locks the user's home directory before sleeping (keys are dropped from memory) and homed freezes the user's session until the home is unlocked with the password again. The re-authentication has to come from outside the user's session, but Plasma Login Manager never reacted to resume, so the frozen session just stayed on screen with no way to unlock it. Now the daemon checks, on logind's PrepareForSleep(false), whether the active user's home is locked (homed GetHomeByName) and if so switches to its greeter. Logging in there already goes through PAM (pam_systemd_home unlocks the home and thaws the session) and then reuses the existing session with logind UnlockSession + ActivateSession, so the screen locker unlocks too and no second password is needed.

commits.message:
daemon: Show the greeter after resume when the user's home is locked

With systemd-homed's suspend option the home is locked during sleep and
the session stays frozen, so nothing could ask for the password again.
On resume, show the greeter: logging in there unlocks home and session.

BUG: 488104

media.caption: Master daemon, fake logind + fake systemd-homed: suspend, alice's home gets locked, resume. The daemon does nothing (never even asks homed), so the frozen session would stay on screen
Patched daemon, same steps: it sees alice's home is locked after resume and starts the login greeter (the greeter itself can't run in this test, only the daemon's side)
